name: strip-nondeterminism
desc: Tool for stripping bits of non-deterministic information from files
why: Reproducible-builds tool that rewrites archives and binaries to remove timestamps, a fascinating window into how build artifacts leak state.

brief.what_it_is: strip-nondeterminism is a Perl library that removes non-deterministic information, such as timestamps and filesystem ordering, from various file and archive formats. The homepage describes it as a library, while the brew metadata lists a strip-nondeterminism executable, which I could not confirm from the page. The page does not say what the output looks like beyond the files being stripped of that information.
brief.why_it_exists: The homepage frames it as a way to make build outputs reproducible by stripping the non-deterministic details that builds leak into files. It is integrated into Debian's debhelper(7) build system.
brief.standout: Its main hook is that it plugs directly into Debian's debhelper(7) build system, so package builds get cleaned up as part of the normal build rather than as a separate manual step. The scout note's claim that it rewrites binaries is not supported by the page, which only mentions file and archive formats.
brief.status: Quiet to unknown. The GitLab page shows a creation date of May 15, 2018, but no last-commit date, release date, or recent activity was visible, so I cannot confirm whether it is maintained.
brief.caveats: The homepage is a short project blurb and the README body did not load, so this brief is thin. No commands, install steps, or supported-format list were visible. The only license shown is GNU GPLv3. The brew description calls it a tool, but the page describes a Perl library. The scout note's claim about binaries is unverified.
quotes: StripNondeterminism is a Perl library for stripping non-deterministic information such as timestamps and filesystem ordering from various file and archive formats.
It is integrated into Debian's debhelper(7) build system.
